## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

- Python API or bindings
- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL
- Documentation or samples
- Benchmarks or performance

## Summary

Enable deterministic indexer backward for compact H32 tensors on the default
SM100 backend. The existing CuTeDSL kernel already combines the two required
properties: it pads H32 to its internal M64 tile with predicated compact
stores, and its deterministic mode assigns fixed query-row stripes to
CTA-private dK planes. This change exposes that supported intersection in the
Python capability gate, documents it, and adds focused correctness and
performance coverage.

The `sm100_v2` deterministic backend remains H64-only.

## Why

The production r=4 DSA indexer uses H32. Before this change,
`IndexerBackward(..., deterministic=True)` rejected H32 before launch even
though the default kernel's compact-H32 path and fixed-owner deterministic dK
path are compatible. Callers therefore had no native deterministic path for
this shape.

The new test exercises 194 query rows, which is more than twice the 96
producer planes and forces plane reuse across waves. It covers local and
global top-k indices, FP32 and BF16 dK, TopK512 and TopK2048, eight bitwise
repeat launches, an independent numerical reference, poisoned output and
workspace storage, and canary tails after compact dQ/dW tensors.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

There is no signature change. On SM100/SM103, the default indexer-backward
backend expands its deterministic envelope from H64/D128 to H32-or-H64/D128.
The `sm100_v2` deterministic envelope remains H64/D128. Existing ordinary and
H64 deterministic behavior is unchanged.

The deterministic implementation retains the existing 96 dense FP32 dK
planes, so its caller-owned workspace is
`96 * B * S_k * D * sizeof(float)`, aligned by the existing helper. A single
GB200 measurement of the compact-H32 path with B=1, D128, TopK512, global
indices, five warmups, 20 CUDA-event samples, reused outputs/workspace, and a
256 MiB L2 flush measured:

| Global context / CP | Local Q / compressed K | Ordinary | Deterministic | Ratio | Ordinary run max allocation | Deterministic run max allocation | Workspace |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256K / 64 | 4,096 / 65,536 | 272.42 us | 1,423.98 us | 5.23x | 0.65 GiB | 3.65 GiB | 3.00 GiB |
| 256K / 32 | 8,192 / 65,536 | 510.51 us | 1,984.56 us | 3.89x | 0.97 GiB | 3.97 GiB | 3.00 GiB |
| 1M / 64 | 16,384 / 262,144 | 1,397.41 us | 5,656.59 us | 4.05x | 1.85 GiB | 13.85 GiB | 12.00 GiB |

The max-allocation columns are process peaks from the benchmark harness and
include its compact/H64 validation buffers and L2 flush tensor. The incremental
deterministic allocation equals the reported workspace.

The deterministic cost is dominated by clearing 96 full dK planes and
reducing them in fixed order; this PR does not change that algorithm.

## Testing

GPU validation used one GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13.0, cuDNN backend 9.19, PyTorch
2.8 development build, and CuTe DSL 4.7.1.

```bash
pytest -q \
  test/python/deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_backward.py::test_DSA_indexer_backward_deterministic_compact_h32
# 3 passed, 4 warnings in 13.91s

pytest -m "L0 or L1" \
  test/python/deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_backward.py \
  -k "deterministic and not topk2048_boundary and not repeat1000" -q
# 28 passed, 4 warnings in 33.28s

pre-commit run --files \
  benchmark/dsa/README.md \
  benchmark/dsa/benchmark_dsa_indexer_h32.py \
  docs/fe-oss-apis/dsa.md \
  python/cudnn/deepseek_sparse_attention/indexer_backward/api.py \
  test/python/deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_backward.py
# passed

cd docs/fern
npx --yes fern-api check
# 0 errors, 1 warning

git diff --check upstream/develop...HEAD
# passed
```

The benchmark table above used the following command for each listed local
shape, once without and once with `--deterministic`:

```bash
python -m benchmark.dsa.benchmark_dsa_indexer_h32 \
  --batch 1 --seqlen-q <local-q> --seqlen-k <compressed-k> \
  --topk 512 --topk-indices-global --warmup 5 --repeats 20 \
  [--deterministic]
```

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `f49d7bdeb82d` against base `7701e232c2b8`.

Thank you for your contribution! The default-backend H32 admission is consistent with the existing compact loads/stores and fixed-owner dK implementation. Independent native checks found no runtime blocker, and sm100_v2 still rejects H32. The new numerical test needs its loss normalization corrected; its current broad tolerance conceals a factor-of-two mismatch.

**[P2] Match the numerical reference to the test's batch-normalized loss** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/f49d7bdeb82db952f80b85184f6b9f6c045f3775/test/python/deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_backward.py#L1199))

This case uses B=2 and loss_coeff=S_q, so the wrapper correctly applies loss_coeff/(B*S_q)=0.5. The reference below instead uses grad_scale=1.0. All three new cases therefore compare half-sized gradients against the unit-scale reference, yet pass because the helper allows RMS relative error up to 0.55 and cosine similarity ignores overall scale. Set loss_coeff to B*S_q (or pass the actual 0.5 scale to the reference), and give this case a magnitude bound that rejects a factor-of-two control. The repeatability and canary checks remain useful; this is a test-oracle issue, not evidence of incorrect kernel scaling.

Evidence: Measured all three new cases on native SM100: dQ/dW/dK norm ratios versus the current reference are approximately 0.5000 and RMS relative errors are 0.49965–0.49998, while the unchanged test passes. With a matching 0.5-scale reference, the same outputs have RMS relative errors 0.00313–0.00445. Attribution: Independently identified from the new B=2 test and confirmed by native output/reference measurements.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100, PyTorch 2.11 and CuTe DSL 4.7: 28 selected deterministic tests passed, including all three new H32 cases. Their numerical-oracle limitation is described above. The three H32 cases also passed Compute Sanitizer racecheck with eight repeated launches each and 0 reported hazards. Separate H32 checks used matching loss normalization with 96/128/148 producer planes, TopK512/128/2048, and local/global IDs. All three cases passed 18 CUDA-graph replays across changed inputs, preserved dQ/dW/workspace canaries, and stayed within 0.00431 RMS relative error of the independent autograd reference. The old API rejects these H32 declarations; the new default API accepts them, and sm100_v2 still rejects them. Ran the updated benchmark at B=1, S_q=4096, S_k=65536, TopK512 with global IDs on a separate 148-SM SM100 engineering device. Its compact/padded numerical comparison passed. Twelve warmed, L2-flushed samples gave compact medians of about 0.445 ms ordinary and 2.565 ms deterministic; deterministic eager H64 padding measured 2.729 ms. The deterministic workspace and incremental process peak allocation were both exactly 3 GiB.

Limitations: SM103 was not executed natively. The performance result is one workload on an engineering device, with deterministic samples ranging from 2.22 to 3.11 ms; it does not reproduce the author's GB200 table or establish a general speedup.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

Independently halving each of the three gradients in each case causes the revised magnitude check to fail: all nine negative controls were rejected. Reused the prior unchanged-runtime validation: 28 deterministic tests, three racecheck cases with zero hazards, and three additional capture/producer-plane cases with 18 replays. Those results apply to the unchanged implementation; only the three corrected tests and their magnitude controls were rerun on this head.

Limitations: SM103 remains untested natively; the previously reported engineering-device performance measurements retain their original scope.

Comment only: this PR already has an active approval; preserving existing approvals.

@@ -195,6 +195,17 @@ python -m benchmark.dsa.benchmark_dsa_indexer_h32

 ```

 ### Sparse Attention Forward
 
 `benchmark_dsa_sparse_attention_forward.py` benchmarks the public SM100

@@ -24,23 +24,38 @@
 
 import argparse
 import json
+import math
 import statistics
 
 import torch
 
 from cudnn import DSA
+from cudnn.deepseek_sparse_attention.indexer_backward.deterministic_dk_sm100 import deterministic_dk_workspace_bytes
 
 
-def _make_case(batch: int, seqlen_q: int, seqlen_k: int, topk: int, seed: int):
+def _make_case(batch: int, seqlen_q: int, seqlen_k: int, topk: int, seed: int, topk_indices_global: bool):
     """Allocate deterministic compact-H32 inputs and sparse-score operands."""
+    if topk > seqlen_k:
+        raise ValueError(f"topk ({topk}) must not exceed seqlen_k ({seqlen_k})")
     generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda")
     generator.manual_seed(seed)
     q32 = torch.randn((batch, seqlen_q, 32, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator)
     w32 = torch.randn((batch, seqlen_q, 32), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator)
     k = torch.randn((batch, seqlen_k, 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator)
     attn = torch.randn((batch, seqlen_q, topk), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, generator=generator)
     predict = torch.softmax(torch.randn(attn.shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, generator=generator), dim=-1)
-    indices = torch.randint(0, seqlen_k, attn.shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32, generator=generator)
+    # Deterministic dK requires distinct valid IDs in each semantic top-k row.
+    # An affine permutation avoids materializing one S_k-wide random tensor per
+    # query while retaining a dispersed gather pattern at production lengths.
+    index_stride = max(1, seqlen_k // topk)
+    while math.gcd(index_stride, seqlen_k) != 1:
+        index_stride += 1
+    starts = torch.randint(0, seqlen_k, (batch, seqlen_q, 1), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64, generator=generator)
+    positions = torch.arange(topk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64).view(1, 1, topk)
+    indices = ((starts + positions * index_stride) % seqlen_k).to(torch.int32)
+    if topk_indices_global:
+        batch_offsets = torch.arange(batch, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view(batch, 1, 1) * seqlen_k
+        indices += batch_offsets
 
     return q32, w32, k, attn, predict, indices

     )

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `f49d7bdeb82d` against base `7701e232c2b8`.

Thank you for your contribution! The default-backend H32 admission is consistent with the existing compact loads/stores and fixed-owner dK implementation. Independent native checks found no runtime blocker, and sm100_v2 still rejects H32. The new numerical test needs its loss normalization corrected; its current broad tolerance conceals a factor-of-two mismatch.

**[P2] Match the numerical reference to the test's batch-normalized loss** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/f49d7bdeb82db952f80b85184f6b9f6c045f3775/test/python/deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_backward.py#L1199))

This case uses B=2 and loss_coeff=S_q, so the wrapper correctly applies loss_coeff/(B*S_q)=0.5. The reference below instead uses grad_scale=1.0. All three new cases therefore compare half-sized gradients against the unit-scale reference, yet pass because the helper allows RMS relative error up to 0.55 and cosine similarity ignores overall scale. Set loss_coeff to B*S_q (or pass the actual 0.5 scale to the reference), and give this case a magnitude bound that rejects a factor-of-two control. The repeatability and canary checks remain useful; this is a test-oracle issue, not evidence of incorrect kernel scaling.

Evidence: Measured all three new cases on native SM100: dQ/dW/dK norm ratios versus the current reference are approximately 0.5000 and RMS relative errors are 0.49965–0.49998, while the unchanged test passes. With a matching 0.5-scale reference, the same outputs have RMS relative errors 0.00313–0.00445. Attribution: Independently identified from the new B=2 test and confirmed by native output/reference measurements.

Validation: Exact-head native SM100, PyTorch 2.11 and CuTe DSL 4.7: 28 selected deterministic tests passed, including all three new H32 cases. Their numerical-oracle limitation is described above. The three H32 cases also passed Compute Sanitizer racecheck with eight repeated launches each and 0 reported hazards. Separate H32 checks used matching loss normalization with 96/128/148 producer planes, TopK512/128/2048, and local/global IDs. All three cases passed 18 CUDA-graph replays across changed inputs, preserved dQ/dW/workspace canaries, and stayed within 0.00431 RMS relative error of the independent autograd reference. The old API rejects these H32 declarations; the new default API accepts them, and sm100_v2 still rejects them. Ran the updated benchmark at B=1, S_q=4096, S_k=65536, TopK512 with global IDs on a separate 148-SM SM100 engineering device. Its compact/padded numerical comparison passed. Twelve warmed, L2-flushed samples gave compact medians of about 0.445 ms ordinary and 2.565 ms deterministic; deterministic eager H64 padding measured 2.729 ms. The deterministic workspace and incremental process peak allocation were both exactly 3 GiB.

Limitations: SM103 was not executed natively. The performance result is one workload on an engineering device, with deterministic samples ranging from 2.22 to 3.11 ms; it does not reproduce the author's GB200 table or establish a general speedup.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
